title: The Naibbe cipher: a substitution cipher that encrypts Latin and Italian as Voynich Manuscript-like ciphertext
summary: Greshko publishes a hand-executable verbose homophonic cipher with reproducible tables, code and reference ciphertexts. The cipher respaces a plaintext letter stream into units of one or two letters and substitutes glyph strings selected from six tables.
established: Across multiple Latin and Italian inputs, the published cipher produces reversible ciphertext with a number of Voynich-like local statistics, including low conditional character entropy and similar token lengths.

The reference tables were designed from aggregate Currier B frequencies. The construction has limited vocabulary coverage, lacks an explicit line- or paragraph-position rule, and misses the manuscript's long-range correlations in the reported random-walk test.

open.question: Can a fixed Naibbe-style procedure generate the manuscript's line- and paragraph-position preferences while retaining reversible encryption and its local statistical match?
open.check: Declare the cipher and layout rules first, then measure glyph-position effects on independent historical plaintexts and report ambiguity and any losses in the other metrics.
